name: Abyssal Ghost Manta
desc: A shadow some nine metres across with nothing above it that could account for one, and no measurable mass on any instrument that has been pointed at it. It has never finished becoming a manta and shows no sign of intending to; Sector registries carry it as a phenomenon rather than a specimen, which suits everyone involved.

name: Abyssal Irisfin
desc: A thousand eyes open and close in no order and never all at once. Ratings who have gutted one report the pattern continues afterwards, on the inside.

name: Abyssal Gazer
desc: A single eye the size of a fist, slotted crosswise like a goat's, set in a body that could not otherwise be less remarkable. It holds a gaze longer than anything without a mind has business holding one, and crews who have worked a shift under it tend to request reassignment without ever explaining why.

name: Abyssal Necrophyte
desc: Arrives already decaying and stops at roughly half, the rot holding at a stage no chemistry aboard can arrest or advance. Whatever pattern the ghost reached for down there had been dead a long time before anyone thought to go looking for it.

name: Abyssal Eyestar
desc: Five arms, six pupils, and no agreement between them as to where the centre of the animal lies. It holds its shape while observed and loses interest in doing so when it is not, which has made establishing a mass for the record a matter of some argument.

name: Abyssal Razorback Shrimp
desc: Flint-grey and segmented well past the count its length allows, several of those segments being demonstrably the same segment encountered twice. The edges are sharper than the structure carrying them should be able to support, and the Sector's abyssal survey logs list it among the few specimens that must be stored under restraint.

name: Abyssal Razorclam
desc: Opens along three hinges. Reality permits two, and the third is generally offered by those who study such things as a plain statement of how little the abyss regards the local arrangement.

name: Abyssal Stoneplate Lobster
desc: Plated in a material closer to slag than shell and cold enough to take skin off through a glove. It continues working its claws for a day and a night after every other measure of the animal has stopped, which nobody has yet chosen to investigate closely.

name: Abyssal Venomous Aranea
desc: Neither fish nor arachnid and thoroughly committed to both, with a venom that has defeated three separate attempts at classification. Medical advises against handling it and the galley advises against everything else, and for once the two departments are in agreement.

name: Abyssal Yellowback
desc: The one abyssal specimen that looks very nearly ordinary, which is precisely why experienced crews will not have it aboard. The yellow is not pigment, does not stay on the animal, and has been recovered from bulkheads two compartments away.

name: Abyssal Nautilus
desc: A chambered shell wound inward rather than out, spiralling into itself past the point where there is anywhere left to spiral. Each chamber holds a measure of the abyss it came out of, and none of them drain.

name: Steel Pipechovies
desc: Comes through in bundles of five or six, each one a straight length of dull steel with a mouth at the end and no discernible fins. Whatever the ghost was copying, it was not swimming at the time - the consensus is that it found a ration tin rather than the thing inside it.

name: Roider Mudfish
desc: A bottom-feeder's build and a bottom-feeder's manner, in a place with neither bottom nor mud. Roider crews rate them highly, which is generally taken to say more about roider crews than about the fish.

name: Berylcuda
desc: Green-scaled and hard as the mineral it is named for, carrying a barracuda's jaw on a body built from Domain food-stock records. Two patterns pulled through as one, and neither of them finished.

name: Coudplate Tetra
desc: Plated along the back in overlapping cloud-shaped scutes that would armour it against pressures hyperspace does not have. Collectors pay well for the ones whose plating has come through symmetrical, which is fewer than half.

name: Tiger Sailfish
desc: Trails a dorsal banner longer than its own body, striped in a pattern that exists to be seen by something. What that something was is not on record, and the banner goes on moving for a moment after the animal has stopped.

name: Silver Slipstreamer
desc: Silver, streamlined and already at speed when it comes through, holding a heading as though the slipstream it left were still running underneath it. One of very few specimens that behaves the way its shape suggests it should.

name: Green Bass
desc: Green, blunt and entirely obliging. A ghost with no stronger idea to hold onto settles into a bass, and the Sector's logs are so full of them that several survey outfits have stopped recording the species at all.

name: Jungle Snapper
desc: Small, deep-bodied and marked in reds and greens like something that grew up under a canopy, in a medium that has never had one. The colouring is the first thing to go once it is out of the rupture and the last thing anyone remembers about it.

name: Blue Ochtogon Magifin
desc: Eight fins arranged around a body plated in flat panels, too regular to be coincidence and lit faintly along every seam. No Domain record has been found containing anything resembling it, which puts it in a category of about a dozen specimens Sector-wide.

name: Blue Tang
desc: An untroubled blue that holds longer than most colours manage, the shape appearing to sit comfortably on whatever is wearing it. Reef stock, from reefs that went under with their worlds several centuries ago.

name: Soul Bream
desc: Broad, plain and quiet, and the crews who bring them in will not say why the name attached itself. Something about a bream reads as occupied rather than alive, and no instrument aboard has ever agreed.

name: Venomous Sailfish
desc: Sail-finned and patterned to warn rather than to hide, which turns out to be an accurate advertisement. The spines carry enough to put a rating in a medbay for a week, and the pattern is bright enough that this has happened only rarely.

name: Ole' Carp
desc: Grey, slow and wholly uninterested in resisting anything. Every ship of any age has one somewhere in its logs and no crew has ever remembered acquiring it.

name: Credfish
desc: Flat, hard-edged and stamped along the flank in a repeating figure the eye keeps trying to resolve into a denomination. It is not currency, it is not legal tender in any port in the Sector, and this has stopped precisely nobody from trying to pass one.

name: Long Waller
desc: Two metres of whiskered patience, feeling its way along a riverbed that is not there and has never been there. There is something dogged in it that crews find either endearing or unbearable, with very little ground in between.

name: Shimmerclam
desc: Shut on arrival and shut permanently thereafter, resisting every tool rated for the job. The shell runs through colours it carries no pigment for, which is the only remarkable thing it will ever do.

name: Common Crag Crab
desc: Moves sideways and continues sideways until something stops it, which on a crowded deck takes a while. Ten legs, which is the correct number, and no comfort whatsoever.

name: Volturnian Crab
desc: Blue through the shell rather than across it, and the nearest thing hyperspace has ever produced to genuine Volturnian stock. Worth handling carefully, and worth rather more than the handling costs.

name: Adolescent Pyrcrab
desc: Low, broad and slow to commit to anything, which makes it one of the more manageable specimens aboard. It runs warm to the touch, and warmer the longer it is held, and this is where most crews put it down.

name: Adult Pyrcrab
desc: The same animal grown out, running hot enough to raise blisters through a work glove. Every rating who has seen one describes a different fault in its construction, and each of them is entirely certain the others are mistaken.

name: Eelcat
desc: Long, whiskered, and inclined to knot itself around anything within reach. The knots do not survive inspection as knots, but no other word has been offered.

name: Egg
desc: Hyperspace does not spawn, so this is a shape with no process standing behind it. It has never hatched, is not recorded as having changed in any way, and standing orders on most ships are not to remain in the compartment finding out.

name: Bloody Damsel
desc: An orange bright enough to read as a hazard indicator, and territorial about a territory that does not exist in any frame of reference available. It will square up to machinery many times its size and has never once been observed to reconsider.

name: Goldfish
desc: An ornamental pattern with no food value, no fight and no obvious reason to exist out here, turning up most often on ships whose crews have been thinking about home. Considered a good omen by roughly half the Sector's spacers and a wasted opportunity by the other half.

name: Bluefin Theta
desc: Rises for air in a medium that has none, over and over, at the surface of nothing at all. The blue along the fin is the only part of the animal that ever holds still.

name: Abyssal Rockfish
desc: Squat, heavily spined and green along the belly with something that is not algae, there being nothing out here for algae to grow on. The name is a warning about where it was recovered rather than a description of the animal.

name: Adolescent Razorspine
desc: Thin as a blade and lit along the underside, a depth-trick from depths hyperspace has never possessed. The lights go out one at a time, in order, and nobody has established what the order is.

name: Silver Razorspine
desc: The same pattern grown out and gone metallic, heavy enough to deform equipment rated well above its mass. Whatever the ghost was copying, it took a portion of the ship along with it.

name: Lunacyte
desc: Pale, unhurried and lit from within on a cycle that matches nothing aboard and nothing in the local system. Named by a survey crew that watched one for an entire shift and declined, afterwards, to explain the name.

name: Poison Jelly
desc: Trails filaments considerably longer than the bell could support, and goes on trailing them after the bell itself has stopped. It stings for hours afterwards, and for a good deal longer than that in the memory.

name: Aetherial Jelly
desc: Barely present and barely holding, a shape more suggested than constructed. Handled roughly it comes apart, and the pieces do not remain pieces for long.

name: Mossy Bass
desc: Furred green along the back with something that is not moss, in a place with nothing for moss to take hold of. It fights hard, briefly, and then not at all.

name: Largemouth Bass
desc: Big, blunt and obliging, and the most frequently logged specimen in the Persean Sector by a wide margin. Two recovered together are never quite the same size, and the discrepancy has never gone the same way twice.

name: Larva
desc: A thing arrested between shapes. Reality appears to have let it stand on the grounds that larvae are permitted to be unfinished, which is as close to a ruling as anyone has managed to extract from the phenomenon.

name: Waterpillar
desc: Segmented, ringed, and moving in a wave with nothing available to push against. A land pattern, which raises the question of where a hyperspace ghost encountered one, and nobody has produced an answer worth writing down.

name: Emmerling
desc: Named by the crew that recorded the first one, and the name has held for want of any competing suggestion. No template has ever been identified for it, in Domain records or anywhere since.

name: Volturnian Lobster
desc: Blue-shelled and heavy through the claw, and near enough to the genuine Askonian article to command the genuine price. A good deal of work is being done by near enough, and the trade knows it.

name: Rock Lobster
desc: Grey, unremarkable, and gripping whatever is nearest rather than the other way about. Good eating by the standards available this far out, which is not a demanding standard.

name: Striped Mackerel
desc: Barred, quick and schooling with nothing to school alongside. The bars continue to move after the animal has stopped, which is the point at which most crews stop watching.

name: Marlin
desc: Long bill, long body, and a run that costs equipment. Bringing one in is generally the end of the work for that watch, one way or another.

name: Mussel
desc: Clamped shut around a rock that did not come through with it. Whatever the pattern believes it is holding onto is not aboard, and the grip does not slacken.

name: Deep Terror
desc: Eight arms, deep red, and considerably better coordinated than most of the crew observing it. It gets into things, which is a serious problem given what it is made of.

name: Yellow King
desc: Alters its colouring against a background nobody else can perceive, and conducts itself on deck as though owed something specific. Extended exposure is discouraged in the standing orders of at least two survey outfits.

name: Pacu Pacu
desc: Blunt, flat-toothed, and disconcertingly human about the mouth. The teeth are the part of the pattern that came through cleanest, which is not the part anyone would have chosen.

name: Perch
desc: Striped, spiny and entirely ordinary in every respect that can be measured. Most watches, that is a relief.

name: Pomfret
desc: Silver, deep-bodied and holding its shape better than most, which makes it a common first specimen for a new crew. It is also, by a considerable margin, the one they are least able to describe afterwards.

name: Hyperprawn
desc: Translucent, thumb-length and arriving by the hundred. One is nothing worth recording; several hundred turning together in the same instant is a different matter, and the logs reflect it.

name: Pufferfish
desc: Arrives slack and unimpressive, having apparently concluded that the danger has passed. It has not.

name: Ballooner
desc: The same animal with its mind made up - inflated, spined and declining to come back down by any means available. Reality permits the volume and is plainly unhappy about where the volume came from.

name: Deepwater Pufferfish
desc: Blue, spined, and already inflated on the way through, as though something down there had startled it. Nothing had, according to every instrument that was watching at the time.

name: Silver Star
desc: Winged, silver, and gliding on a medium with nothing whatsoever to glide upon. Whatever pattern this one reached for was not in any Domain database, and the Sector's xeno-survey people have been politely uninterested for some years now.

name: Gargantuan Waller
desc: A waller grown past all sense, heavy-headed and badly wrong about its own proportions. It reads as an ordinary catfish right up until somebody measures it, and then it takes two ratings and a winch.

name: Nemo
desc: Banded orange and white and sealed in a bag of water that nobody aboard put it in. The bag came through the rupture with the animal, holds pressure, and has so far resisted every attempt to determine what it is made of.

name: Curious Damsel
desc: Small, bright, and inclined to follow machinery back rather than flee it. Curiosity is not something a hyperspace ghost is supposed to be capable of, and the survey literature is quietly uncomfortable about this one.

name: Flarefin Koi
desc: Fins like a flare going off, trailing light that illuminates nothing at all around it. Ornamental stock from a garden nobody has been able to place, on a world nobody has been able to name.

name: Undersea Bee
desc: Thumbnail-sized, barely coherent, and arriving in swarms or not at all. The swarm behaves as a single animal, which is not a thing any of the individual specimens are structurally capable of.

name: Stinkfish
desc: The smell arrives first and outlasts the specimen by several days. No compound has been isolated, no filter has proved effective, and morale aboard has never once improved during the attempt.

name: Blue Sea Tuna
desc: Big, blue, and built to cross an ocean in a place that has never held one. It makes the crossing regardless, at speed, in whatever direction it happened to be pointed.

name: Rainbow Carp
desc: Ornamental, and patterned in colours ship's screens render only approximately. Worth a great deal more to a collector than to a galley, which is the whole of its value.

name: Blind Crawler
desc: Eyeless, feeling its way along the bottom of a place that does not have one, and sounding a low note it requires water to produce. It produces the note anyway, and continues producing it well after arrival.

name: Red Snapper
desc: Deep red, sharp-toothed and a genuine fight from start to finish. One of the few specimens worth recording for its own sake rather than for the tally.

name: Coach
desc: Small, silver and everywhere, named by somebody who found it funnier than the rest of the crew did. A rupture that yields nothing else is logged as a poor showing.

name: Sufur Diver
desc: Mottled yellow, reeking of sulphur, and inclined to hold its position rather than run from anything. It outlasts pursuit rather than outpacing it, which works more often than it has any right to.

name: Storm Salmon
desc: Runs against a current that is not there, hard and in one direction, trailing charge the entire way. What it is running towards has not been established, and several people have spent longer on the question than the question deserves.

name: Shad
desc: Thin, silver schooling stock with no school available to join. It arrives alone and conducts itself as though it were among thousands.

name: Silverback
desc: Heavy through the shoulder and silver along the spine, throwing itself clear of a surface that does not exist. A hazard to equipment, and on two recorded occasions to the crew standing near it.

name: Skate
desc: Flat, winged, and gliding on nothing at all. It passes over machinery rather than through it, a distinction the machinery is not equipped to appreciate.

name: Skelleton
desc: A fish pattern with everything except the bones omitted, and the name misspelled on the first survey sheet and every sheet since. Reality accepted the skeleton and declined the rest, and the result moves regardless.

name: Spined Loach
desc: Small, whiskered, and armed beneath the eye with a spine that catches on absolutely everything. More trouble than the specimen is worth, and the trade prices it accordingly.

name: Mind Flayer
desc: Jets in a medium that offers nothing to push against, and moves anyway. Crews who work a long watch near one report the same thought arriving twice, some minutes apart, and do not care to elaborate.

name: Crysal Aberration
desc: Faceted, rigid, and lit from within in a colour that does not appear on the manifest. Whatever it is aberrating from, the survey record is clear that it is not coming back.

name: Giant Squid
desc: Deep red, long-armed and inking freely, which becomes a problem when the ink declines to stay where it lands. Standard practice is a bucket, and something underneath the bucket.

name: Banana Star
desc: Five arms, yellow, curved, and jointed in places arms are not jointed. Named by a rating who has since been quietly reassigned to other duties.

name: Crusty Star
desc: Blue, rough as old hull plating, and wholly indifferent to its circumstances. It continues doing whatever it was doing, at the same rate, throughout.

name: Crystal Star
desc: Rigid, faceted, and ringing faintly whenever it is set down on anything hard. The arm-tips are sharp enough that handling one bare-handed appears in safety briefings as an example.

name: Leafy Star
desc: Soft-armed, and regenerating anything removed from it considerably faster than the available material can account for. What the replacement arm is made of remains an open question that nobody is funding.

name: Scraggly Star
desc: Thin-armed, uneven, and short one point - though never the same point on any two specimens. Reality appears to have made an accounting error here and elected to let it stand.

name: Ice Tuna
desc: Heavy, cold through to the core and frosted along the flank, and the best eating in the whole ghost-stock catalogue by a comfortable distance. Worth every bit of the equipment it costs to bring one in.

name: Vulcan Cannonfish
desc: Blunt-nosed and barrel-bodied, built to the proportions of ordnance rather than of anything that ever swam. The ghost reached for the nearest available shape and found the ship's own autocannon, which says something uncomfortable about how the process selects.

name: Amberjack
desc: Fast, yellow along the tail, and a long fight for an animal of its size. Sought out by crews who have grown tired of logging bass, which is most of them eventually.
